disease_label_per_paper: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura detected with oral hemorrhage
presentation_summary: 79-year-old woman presented with spontaneous gingival bleeding around right upper molars that was difficult to control.
She had petechial hemorrhage over the lower legs and intraoral hemorrhagic bullae on both buccal mucosae with tongue ecchymosis; no obvious lymphadenopathy was noted and vital signs were normal.
Admission labs showed platelets 0.2 x10^4/uL (2 x10^9/L), WBC 6800/uL, hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, PT-INR 1.01, APTT 28.5 s, D-dimer 2.9 ug/mL, AST 14 U/L, and ALT 16 U/L.

risk_context.source_text_value: 79-year-old woman with hypertension controlled with benidipine hydrochloride

observations.source_text_value: spontaneous gingival bleeding ... difficult to control and persisted
large hemorrhagic bullae on both sides of the buccal mucosa
petechial hemorrhage over the lower legs
ecchymosis on the dorsum of the tongue

confirmatory_findings.finding: Peripheral smear normal apart from thrombocytopenia
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: A peripheral blood smear revealed no abnormalities in differential leukocyte count or erythrocytic morphology and showed normal-sized platelets.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Bone marrow megakaryocytes increased without morphologic abnormalities
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: A bone marrow examination revealed increased numbers of megakaryocytes without morphologic abnormalities.
The patient was diagnosed with ITP.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Refractory initial therapy and response to thrombopoietin receptor agonist
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Severe thrombocytopenia was refractory to pulsed steroid and high-dose immunoglobulin therapy; a thrombopoietin receptor agonist led to rapid platelet increase.

outcome.source_text_value: Her platelets rapidly increased and no bleeding complications were reported.

quality_warnings: Bone marrow, final diagnosis, and treatment response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Oral bleeding, petechiae, platelet count, preserved WBC/hemoglobin, and normal coagulation are rankable presentation evidence.
